Saudi Arabia’s Diriyah Scraps $191 Million Hotel Build
items.body: Diriyah has canceled a $191 million hotel contract and won’t say why. It’s the first Saudi hotel project known to be pulled since the Houthi strikes on Riyadh, and it comes from one of the few giga-projects still spending.

items.headline: Sabre Wants to Be the Transaction Engine Behind AI Travel Bookings
items.body: AI platforms could become a new front door for travel bookings. Sabre wants to handle the transactions behind them, even if someone else controls the customer relationship.

items.headline: LA-Area Voters Approve Wave of Hotel Tax Hikes Ahead of 2028 Olympics
items.body: A dozen cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties raised or updated lodging taxes in recent elections as cities prepare for a surge in visitors during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

items.headline: Airport Shutdown Wiped 65% Off Riyadh Hotel RevPAR in October
items.body: Riyadh’s hotels lost their peak season when the airport shut. With BA, Cathay Pacific and others suspended into the new year and Houthi strikes still hitting the capital, the recovery hasn’t started.
